playbook.notes: The answers candidate: version 2 (winter) with rules for the deck's wipes and removal and for the threats the engine rules starved, written from the 200 tables of bots of ab-run #28 (seed 20261280: candidate 59 wins, stock pilot 37). There the candidate cast 20 cards in a smaller share of the games they were drawn than stock AI (docs/agents/arm_card_diff.py): every play rule that has something to do goes before Forge's own choice, and the base names only ramp, Winter, the mill engine and a few engines, so Forge was asked last with little mana left. Winter's recasts from the command zone took the mana on 256 of the 1,248 turns a starved card was affordable. WIPES (rules 2 to 5). Deluge of Doom was cast in none of the 111 games it was drawn under either pilot (Forge's AI never casts it) and was in hand at 31 and 41 losses. Its X is the card types in our graveyard, and Winter's end-step trigger exiles the whole graveyard (Forge chooses), so at the start of our turn X was 0 to 1 on 59% of the turns it was in hand; before the end step, after Winter's attack mill, it was 4 or more in 156 of the 179 turns her delirium trigger fired. So rule 3 casts it in the second main phase on a board worth it (an opponent with 6 creatures and more creatures and power than we have; in the losses the largest opposing board had 15 nonland permanents on the seat's last two turns, median, against 6 of ours, and in the wins 8 against 6), and rule 4 in either main phase when an opponent could kill us next turn (threat >= life) with more power than we have. Culling Ritual (destroys every nonland permanent of mana value 2 or less: every token) on the same board (rule 2) and on a lethal threat (rule 5); it costs our cheap rocks, which is why it wants a board worth it. REMOVAL (rule 9): Binding the Old Gods, Putrefy and Convert to Slime after the mill engine; Putrefy and Convert to Slime are cast only if Forge's logic finds a target, which it picks (Binding's chapter I target is Forge's too). Binding was cast in 19 of 42 games drawn under the base, 28 of 38 under stock. THREATS AND EDICTS (rules 13 to 15), after the engines and Deadbridge Chant: Noxious Gearhulk when an opponent has a creature (Forge took its enters trigger at 75 of 76 casts in the exam, always on an opponent's creature, so no trigger rule), Vile Mutilator when we have a token to sacrifice for it and an opponent has a creature, then Hornet Queen, Demolisher Spawn, Giant Adephage, Moldgraf Monstrosity, Professor Onyx, Wrenn and Seven, Ishkanah and Rendmaw, biggest first. Planeswalker abilities stay Forge's. Rule 19 {forge: unnamed} after the base's mill spells: Forge then picks among the cards no rule names (Reanimate, Formless Genesis, whose X is the lands in a graveyard Winter keeps emptying, Inscription of Abundance, Sakura-Tribe Elder, Solemn, the two-drops) and the abilities no rule covers, before the mid creatures and draw spells. Rules 20 to 22: Moldgraf Millipede, Carrion Grub and Ursine Monstrosity with 30 cards in the library (they mill; held below that, rule 26), Grim Flayer and Burnished Hart, then Harmonize and Night's Whisper with 15. CHANGED FROM THE BASE: Demonic Covenant is taken out of the base's engine rule into a rule of its own just before it (rule 10, library >= 20) and held below 20 cards (rule 27): it mills two every end step, and the base seat lost 12 of its 139 losses to an empty library against 3 of 161 for stock. Everything else of the base is kept, in its order, with the new rules between. Arachnogenesis (an instant fog) is left to Forge: the rules act only in our own main phase, where it makes no spiders. Shipped as version 3 on 2026-11-14 from ab-run #36: at 200 tables of bots (seed 20261310, opponents drawn from bots-v2 under their playbooks of 2026-11-13) 65 wins against its stock pilot's 43 (+11.0 points, 95% +3 to +19, exact test 0.011) with the attack left to Forge, the better of the two attacks on these tables (the same rules won 63 with the go-wide attack). What it casts in a share of games 15 points or more below its stock pilot on the same tables, 9 cards: Carrion Grub (33 of 54 games drawn against 37 of 40), Ursine Monstrosity (34 of 53 games drawn against 43 of 46), Solemn Simulacrum (33 of 51 games drawn against 45 of 51), Formless Genesis (31 of 47 games drawn against 40 of 45), Moldgraf Millipede (24 of 45 games drawn against 31 of 43), Arachnogenesis (16 of 32 games drawn against 31 of 46), Professor Onyx (39 of 51 games drawn against 41 of 44), Whispersilk Cloak (36 of 43 games drawn against 40 of 40) and 1 more. It casts 3 cards that much more often (demo-data/playtest/2026-11-14/second-pass/death-toll-forgeattack-card-diff.txt). VERSION 4 (2026-11-21), the candidate `v4`: version 3 with what passed its exam, part by part. HOOKS: after Forge's own attack has been declared, the attackers sent at a player are sent at the opponent that looks most dangerous instead, when that opponent is ahead of the one attacked by five or more and the attack is no worse there: the damage sure to get through whatever is blocked is at least what it was, no more creatures there could block the attackers, and no attacker meets a blocker that would destroy it unless it met one where it was sent (`"aim": "danger"`; an attack that is sure to kill its target stays, and which creatures attack is not changed); and then the creatures that stayed home attack an opponent that has no creature that can block, the most dangerous such opponent first: those that deal damage, have no ability that taps them (or have vigilance) and are not wanted home by Forge's own judgement of the seat's defence (`"open": true`; a weaker opponent is not killed this way while a more dangerous one lives); and then a sure kill is taken from the most dangerous opponent down (`"finish": "leader"`: enough attackers are put on the opponent that looks most dangerous that the damage reaches its life whatever it blocks, then on the next one, and no weaker opponent is killed while a more dangerous one lives); a triggered ability of the seat that removes one permanent of an opponent (destroys it, exiles it, returns it to hand or library) is aimed at the opponent that looks most dangerous, when that opponent looks more dangerous than the one Forge aimed at by five or more and has a permanent of the same kind worth at least as much as Forge's choice or at least 4 (`"targets": {"triggers": "danger"}`); when Forge's blocks leave at least the seat's life in damage unblocked and blocks exist that would not, blocks are added, the least valuable free creatures in front of the heaviest unblocked attackers and only as many as it takes for the seat to live (`"block": {"survive": true}`). SHIPPED 2026-11-21 as version 4. Every part passed its own exam beside version 3 on the same 200 tables at the owner's table (ab-run #46 to #55, seed 20261390; demo-data/ab/2026-11-21-ab-v25/, DESIGN.md section 35): wins of 200 where version 3 won 52: leader 54, aim 58, block 54, swing 56, open 53. No two parts were played together; the version is at the tables beside version 3 in ab-run #57 (seed 20261410). VERSION 5 CANDIDATE `guard` (2026-11-21). Version 4 with one change: after Forge's own attack has been declared and the hooks the version already has have acted, attackers are taken back when the attack leaves the seat where the opponents one after another are sure to kill it before its next turn and keeping them home prevents that, or, when nothing kept home does, where one opponent alone is (`"guard": "table"`; a sure kill's attackers stay, and an attack stands when nothing kept home would save the seat). No cast or trigger rule is changed. SHIPPED 2026-11-22 as version 5: the guard arm of ab-run #57 (seed 20261410, tables that chose nothing; demo-data/ab/2026-11-22-ab-v26/, DESIGN.md section 36). On the same 200 tables at the owner's table, every other seat a version of 2026-11-21: version 3 59 wins, version 4 63 (25 tables against 21, exact test 0.66), version 5 59 (3 against 7 beside version 4, exact test 0.34); deaths with its own creatures tapped 18 under version 4, 18 under version 5. The parts of version 4 were played together here for the first time, and over the ten decks they stand (186 tables against 155, exact test 0.10).
